newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori says Jan-May yr-on-yr growth 7 percent.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori says Jan-May yr-on-yr growth 7 percent.

text.p: Peru's President Alberto Fujimori said year-on-year economic growth between January and May was around seven percent.
The president, in a speech late Thursday, added that Peru's international reserves, should reach $10 billion by mid-July.
Those figures, combined with Peru's 12-month inflation rate of nine percent, were "sufficiently eloquent" to demonstrate the country's sustained growth rate, Fujimori added.
According to previous figures, gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the first four months of the year was 7.3 percent, compared with a 0.7 growth in the January to April period 1996.
Net international reserves were $9.835 billion on June 18.
Fujimori said the imminent $10 billion reserve figure was "a historical record, unimaginable two years ago."

Fujimori also announced a 200 soles ($125) bonus payment to state workers for the July independence holidays, which would total 240 million soles. "It is little, but we have to continue being prudent to maintain the stability of sustained growth," he said.
